answer: Every epoch, each identity must present a fresh cipher signed inside its own hardware enclave: the enclave key is registered once and can sign only one answer per epoch. A farm running ten names on one machine still produces one valid signature per epoch, so the other nine starve — like an onyx vault that opens once per key, while a zephyr of cheap clones passes through with nothing. Cloning the key means buying the hardware again, so cost grows linearly with every fake identity.
